To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the symmetry energy at densities ρ ~ 0.5ρ0 can only be probed in HIC experiments with beams of radioactive nuclei, and that the isospin dependence of the momentum fields must be included in the models to extract the symmetry energy.

the isovector effective mass is a crucial parameter in the description of HIC at E/A>200 MeV, and that the momentum dependence is the main reason why the symmetry energy cannot be directly extracted from the n/p emission ratio, as it has been suggested in the literature.
the isospin dependence of the momentum distribution is a key ingredient in order to extract the symmetry energy at high densities.

the development of a theoretical framework to understand how the nuclear symmetry energy can be extracted from the experimental data of HIC at energies above 100 MeV per nucleon, and how the momentum dependence of nuclear matter can be disentangled from the symmetry energy.

the isospin dependence of the in-medium nucleon effective mass is crucial in the determination of Esym(ρ).
